previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a 58-year-old male with a history of acute myeloid leukemia in remission, chronic graft-versus-host disease, and chronic kidney disease, was admitted with a five-day history of cough, diarrhea, myalgias, and low-grade fevers. He was found to have parainfluenza type 3 infection, with chest imaging showing interstitial lung changes consistent with viral or atypical infection. His kidney function was acutely worsened on admission, likely due to dehydration from poor oral intake and diarrhea, but improved with intravenous fluids. He was managed supportively with oxygen, cough control, and a short course of levofloxacin. Acyclovir was held due to impaired renal function. His symptoms resolved, and he was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to continue hydration, monitor weight, and follow up with his oncologist.
problems: Complications of transplanted organ, stem cell
Secondary diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, not stated as uncontrolled, or unspecified
Lung involvement in other diseases classified elsewhere

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year old man with history of acute 
myeloid leukemia status-post allogeneic cord transplant ___ ___ 
complicated by graft-versus-host disease, stage III chronic 
kidney disease, and secondary hemochromatosis with iron 
overload, who presented with several days of nonbloody diarrhea, 
nausea, vomiting, found to have adenovirus gastroenteritis, 
hospital course complicated by perirectal abscess, pneumonia, 
and pulmonary edema requiring 6 days of intubation. 

# Adenovirus Gastroenteritis: Differential for the patient's 
nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea included norovirus, CMV, EBV, 
adenovirus, HHV6, microspora, isospora, enterovirus, influenza, 
adenovirus, Cdiff (although unlikely given Cdiff negative), GVHD 
(although patient had no history of gut GVHD) and 
mycophenolate-induced colitis. Patient presented with Cr of 4.4 
(elevated from baseline 2.3-2.5) and bicarbonate of 10 and he 
received IVF and sodium bicarbonate repletion and his Cr 
returned to baseline and metabolic acidosis was corrected. GI 
was consulted and performed a flexible sigmoidoscopy and EGD 
with biopsies of intestinal mucosa which showed no GVHD. 
Adenovirus returned positive ___ both the blood and stool, 
confirming the diagnosis. Patient received 1 dose of cidofovir 
0.5 mg/kg on ___ and adenovirus became undetectable ___ blood. 
He also received IVIG on ___, and ___. IgG on ___. 
Patient was made NPO as he was not tolerating PO intake due to 
ongoing nausea and vomiting. Total parenteral nutrition was 
given supplemented with folate (started on ___, multivitamin 
with minerals, and zinc given low zinc of 31; VitD level low at 
28, increased Vit D supplementation to 50,000U weekly on ___, 
and he received 5 weekly doses at this amount. His diet was 
advanced as tolerated and he was weaned off TPN at the end of 
his ICU stay. The patient was treated with Reglan 5mg QID to 
help with his nausea. Reglan was tapered off prior to hospital 
discharge. Zinc and copper levels were rechecked on ___ and 
zinc was slightly low, so nutrition recommended zinc sulfate 
220mg daily x 10 days (starting on ___. Zinc level should be 
rechecked after 10 days of therapy. On the day of discharge, he 
was eating regular meals without nausea or vomiting. 

# Perirectal Abscess: Patient has history of perirectal abscess 
and, ___ the setting of frequent diarrhea, developed erythema, 
tenderness and induration along old scar line on left buttock 
cheek and a new fluid collection was identified on ultrasound. 
He underwent incision and drainage of the perirectal abscess by 
surgery on ___. He received daptomycin and zosyn (renally 
dosed) to cover for skin/soft tissue and enteric organisms. The 
wound healed nicely.

# Multifocal Pneumonia: The patient developed a cough and slowly 
increasing hypoxia during his hospital course. It was initially 
felt to be related to his underlying lung disease (BOOP) as well 
as adenovirus infection, but symptoms worsened despite clearance 
of the virus. The patient spiked a fever on ___ so his coverage 
was broadened from ___ to ___ ___ case 
of fungal PNA. A CT chest showed multifocal PNA. The patient 
then had sudden respiratory decompensation on the floor after an 
episode of post-tussive emesis and was ___ transferred to 
the ICU, intubated on arrival. He underwent bronchoscopy and 
cultures were all negative. He received 3 days of stress dose 
steroids. No evidence of MRSA and as such vancomycin was d/c'ed. 
His voriconazole was discontinued on ___ for negative fungal 
markers. He received IV diuresis and eventually autodiuresed 
with good effect. He completed an 8 day course of meropenem and 
was successfully extubated. After broad-spectrum antibiotics 
were discontinued, the patient was started on prophylactic 
fluconazole, Bactrim, and acyclovir. The patient felt great 
cough relief with nebulized ipratropium, so he was discharged 
with a nebulizer machine and a prescription for ipratropium.

# Decompensated Systolic Heart Failure: The patient has a 
history of systolic heart failure with an ejection fraction of 
25% (confirmed on ___ echo). He had not been on diuretics at 
home. During his hospital course, he developed pulmonary edema 
which was likely part of the reason he had respiratory failure. 
He was treated with a Lasix drip while ___ the ICU. On the floor, 
diuresis was continued with Lasix 80mg PO once to twice daily. 
Weight on day of discharge 234.2 lbs. The patient was discharged 
with a prescription for Lasix 80mg PO daily. He was continued on 
carvedilol at home dose as well as aspirin 81mg daily. He will 
need repeat Chem-7 and volume assessment at his follow-up 
appointments. We will ask for TeleHealth for heart failure 
management from the patient's visiting nursing service. The 
patient has follow-up with his cardiologist (Dr. ___ on 
___.

# Acute on Chronic Kidney Injury: Cr up to 4.4 on admission from 
recent baseline of ___ on admission, likely prerenal ___ 
setting of nausea/vomiting/diarrhea/poor PO intake. Cr returned 
to baseline with IV fluid repletion. Cr remained between 2.7 and 
2.9 after receiving cidofovir. The patient's creatinine bumped 
up again when he was transferred to the unit, and peaked at 4.4. 
Renal was consulted and noted muddy brown casts ___ the urine, 
consistent with a diagnosis of Acute Tubular Necrosis. 
Creatinine trended down with diuresis. Creatinine on the day of 
discharge was 3.3 and had been stable there for the 3 days prior 
to discharge. The patient has follow-up with his nephrologist 
(Dr. ___ on ___.

# Macrocytic Anemia: The patient has a history of macrocytic 
anemia with a hemoglobin of about 11. During this admission, his 
hemoglobin drifted down into the mid-7s and MCV rose to 115. 
Reticulocyte index was low at 0.6%. Hemolysis labs were 
negative. Folate and B12 were normal. TSH normal at 2.7. 
Differential diagnosis includes parvovirus versus 
myelodysplastic syndrome. The patient was highly encouraged to 
have a bone marrow biopsy prior to discharge home, but he 
adamently refused. He should have repeat CBC checked at his 
oncology follow up appointment, and if counts remain low, 
consider bone marrow biopsy. The patient has serum parvovirus 
pending at the time of discharge.

# Elevated Human Herpes Virus 6: The patient had HHV6 checked 
frequently throughout hospitalization and the level peaked at 
992 on ___. The patient was not treated. A repeat level was 
drawn on the day of the discharge and was pending at discharge. 
His levels should continue to be trended ___ the outpatient 
setting. Consider treatment if levels continue to rise.   

#Pancytopenia: Patient with pancytopenia on admission likely 
related to acute viral illness. Repeat chimerism revealed 100% 
donor cells. Counts began to recover with virus treatment. 
Please see anemia above regarding further work-up for hgb which 
never recovered.

#AML: Patient is s/p allogeneic cord stem cell transplant ___ 
___ ___ remission with complications of chronic 
graft-versus-host disease (manifested as arthralgias), stage III 
CKD, and secondary hemochromatosis requiring phlebotomy. 
Mycophenolate was held ___ setting of viremia and the patient was 
discharged off of this medication. He was continued on acyclovir 
and bactrim ppx. He was started on fluconazole for fungal 
prophylaxis. Bactrim was switched over to single strength daily 
dosing for ease of administration (instead of DS three times 
weekly). The patient's ferritin was checked and was found to be 
quite elevated at 6539. Consider chelation therapy as an

#Hypertension: Patient was continued on home carvedilol (with 
holding parameters)

#Depression: Escitalopram was initially held ___ the setting of 
inability to take PO intake but was restarted after 
pseudoseizure on ___.

Level of Consciousness: Alert and interactive.
Activity Status: Ambulatory - requires assistance or aid (walker 
or cane).

 
Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

It was a pleasure taking care of you at ___. You were admitted 
with nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, and a cough.  You were found to 
have adenovirus.  You received one dose of cidofovir which 
cleared the adenovirus.  You developed a wound around your 
rectum due to the diarrhea and this was drained by surgery.  
Your diet was advanced slowly as you were able to tolerate, but 
you did require nutrition through an IV for a time. Despite 
treatment of the adenovirus, you continued to have a strong 
cough, then developed a fever. A CT scan of your lungs showed a 
pneumonia so we added an anti-fungal medicine to your 
antibiotics ___ case of a fungal pneumonia. Unfortunately your 
cough worsened and you ended up needing to be on a ventilator ___ 
the ICU for 6 days. Samples of the infection ___ your lung were 
taken at that time and surprisingly no bacteria, virus, or 
fungus grew from the samples. The antibiotics were stopped one 
by one. You were treated with powerful diuretics (""water pills"") 
___ the ICU to help your body pee out excess fluid. You were 
successfully taken off the ventilator and were moved back to the 
Bone Marrow Transplant floor on ___. We continued to give you 
Lasix to remove excess fluid and your cough and oxygen 
requirement decreased. You'll continue to take Lasix at home and 
will need follow-up labs within 1 week to check on your kidneys 
and blood counts. We'll have you assessed for ""TeleHealth"" to 
monitor your heart function directly from home!

We stopped your CellCept on admission to the hospital and you 
should NOT resume taking this medication at home. It puts you at 
too high of risk for infections. We also changed your Bactrim 
medication to once daily dosing to make it easier to remember to 
take. You'll take fluconazole to help prevent fungal infections. 
We're also prescribing a nebulizer machine to help with your 
cough. 

Due to your history of heart failure, it is important that you 
weigh yourself every morning, call MD if weight goes up more 
than 3 lbs. Your weight on the day we discharged you from the 
hospital was: 234.2 pounds

IMPRESSION:

No hydronephrosis, renal stones or masses.  Left urinary jet not clearly
visualized, however no secondary signs to suggest obstruction.

AP CHEST, 10:30 P.M. ON ___   

HISTORY:  ___ man with a cough.

IMPRESSION:  AP chest compared to ___:

Peribronchial opacification at the base of the right lung is new, whether this
is aspiration, atelectasis or early pneumonia is radiographically
indeterminate at this stage.  With a deeper breath, it could resolve. 
Borderline cardiomegaly is stable.  Pulmonary vasculature is borderline
engorged, but there is no pulmonary edema or appreciable pleural effusion.  No
pneumothorax.  Mediastinal widening due in part to vascular engorgement and
fat deposition, not appreciably changed.

PICC LINE PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  IV access needed for IV access.

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGISTS:  Dr. ___ and Dr. ___ performed the procedure.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the patent and
compresible right basilic vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance
using a micropuncture set. Ultrasound images were obtained before and
immediately after establishing intravenous access and saved to PACS.  A
peel-away sheath was then placed over a guidewire and a double lumen PICC line
measuring 37 cm in length was then placed through the peel-away sheath with
its tip positioned in the SVC under fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of the
catheter was confirmed by a fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided ___
double lumen PICC line placement via the right basilic venous approach.  Final
internal length is 37 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC.  The line is ready
to use.

Comparison made to prior study of ___ at 1208.

Portable AP chest film ___ at 1057 is submitted.

IMPRESSION:

Right subclavian PICC line is unchanged in position.  Lung volumes remain
somewhat diminished, and there is some crowding of the perihilar vasculature. 
There are patchy bibasilar opacities which could represent atelectasis in the

INDICATION:  History of AML status post cord transplant several years ago. 
Now spiking fevers and with cough.

COMPARISON:  Chest CT from ___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired through the chest without the
administration of intravenous contrast material.  Multiplanar reformats were
performed, including maximum intensity projection axial images.

TOTAL DLP:  523 mGy-cm.

FINDINGS:  The visualized portion of the thyroid gland is unremarkable.  There
is a right-sided PICC terminating in the mid SVC.  Prominent right
paratracheal lymph nodes measure up to 14 mm, slightly increased in size
compared to the prior study from ___.  The largest 14-mm node
demonstrates a normal fatty hilum, however.  There are no pathologically
enlarged hilar or axillary lymph nodes.  The thoracic aorta is normal in
caliber.  Scattered aortic calcifications are seen.  The right ventricular
outflow tract is normal in caliber.  The heart is normal in size.  The
intracardiac blood pool is relatively hypodense compared to the myocardium,
suggestive of anemia.  There is a small non-hemorrhagic pericardial effusion,
likely physiologic.

This study was not optimized for evaluation of the subdiaphragmatic contents. 
The patient is status post cholecystectomy.  Hyperdensity of the liver likely
relates to prior transfusions.

There are moderate to large bilateral non-hemorrhagic pleural effusions. 
There is subsegmental associated compressive atelectasis in both upper and
lower lobes.  Mixed ground-glass and consolidative peribronchovascular
opacities are seen within both upper lobes, right greater than left (4:24),
likely infectious in nature.  An additional area of consolidative
opacification at the right lung apex is also likely infectious in nature
(6:53).  The tracheobronchial tree is patent to the segmental level
bilaterally.

BONE WINDOW:  No suspicious lytic or blastic lesions are identified. 
Multilevel degenerative changes of the thoracolumbar spine are noted.  There
is ossification of the anterior longitudinal ligament.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Findings compatible with right greater than left upper lobe pneumonia,
likely atypical in nature, although a fungal etiology is not favored given its
imaging appearance.

2.  Bilateral moderate-to-large non-hemorrhagic pleural effusions.
